title: Compress PDF to 150 KB: Make a 150 KB PDF Free, No Upload
description: Make a 150 KB PDF from a larger scan: two to four pages with readable text and a checked size. Compression runs in your browser, so documents stay private.
intro: Use this page when a form wants a 150 KB PDF. Each scanned page is redrawn only as much as needed to land under 150 KB, so text keeps as much sharpness as that size allows.

steps.name: Open your scan
steps.text: Choose the PDF; password-protected files must be unlocked first.

steps.name: Keep the 150 KB chip
steps.text: It is selected for you, next to the other common limits.

steps.name: Start compressing
steps.text: A progress bar counts the pages while each one is redrawn as a JPEG page.

steps.name: Check and download
steps.text: Look at the preview, confirm the size tick, and save the new PDF.

faq.q: Is 150 KB enough for a readable certificate?
faq.a: Yes for one or two pages. Printed text, signatures and round stamps stay clear at normal zoom.

faq.q: What happens if 150 KB is impossible?
faq.a: You see the smallest size reached, for example 210 KB. Remove a page or use a bigger limit if your form allows it.
No. Each page keeps its original width and height; only the picture inside is stored more efficiently.

faq.q: Is my PDF uploaded to a server?
faq.a: No. The PDF is opened, redrawn and saved inside your browser. It never leaves your device, and the page keeps working offline after your first visit.

sections.h2: Forms that work well with 150 KB
paras: A 150 KB cap appears on some university and state government forms for papers like a degree certificate, an experience letter or a character certificate. It is also a sensible middle target for NTA uploads: CSIR NET accepts its category certificate and result-awaited attestation form as PDFs of 50 to 300 KB, and a 150 KB file keeps two pages crisp while staying far from either edge.

sections.h2: How many pages fit in 150 KB
paras: Two to four. At 100 DPI a clean scanned page takes around 40 to 100 KB, so two pages fit with quality to spare; at 72 DPI, three or four plain pages can squeeze in. A two-sided mark sheet plus a cover letter is a typical 150 KB document. Six or more pages usually will not fit, and you are told how close it got.

Delete pages the form did not ask for, such as a blank reverse side or an instructions sheet; removing one page buys more clarity than any setting. If your scanner app has a "document" or black-and-white mode, use it: it removes paper texture before the file ever reaches this tool. A typed PDF over 150 KB is usually heavy because of an embedded logo or font, and compressing it means its text turns into an image.
Your form has a different limit? Open that size, or the PDF resize hub to type any number. Starting from photos instead of a PDF? Making the PDF from the photos gives sharper pages.
